These nutrients originate in the plant biomass (Šamonil et al., 2020) or, in the case of nitrogen, are fixed from the atmosphere by deadwood bacteria (Rinne et al., 2017; Tláskal et al., 2021) and enter topsoil after full deadwood decomposition. Deadwood is also one of the most important factors contributing to the maintenance of biodiversity in forests (Stokland et al., 2012; Seibold et al., 2015). Namely, it is a habitat and a nutrient source for a wide range of organisms, including microorganisms, fungi and bacteria (Johnston et al., 2016; Vˇetrovský et al., 2020; Tláskal and Baldrian, 2021). Due to filamentous growth, possession of extracellular enzymes and the ability to acidify their substrate, fungi are efficient in the colonization of large patches of wood and its utilization, despite the recalcitrance, fluctuating moisture content and low nitrogen content of this substrate.

Antwortvariable.evidence_anchor: Although there are known problems related to the use of hunting statistics as population indexes (Hornell Willebrand et al. 2006, Ranta et al. 2008), several comparisons of census data and hunting bag statistics suggested largely similar conclusions from both data sources (Baines and Hudson 1995, Cattadori et al. 2003, Imperio et al. 2010 Knauer et al. 2010). Thus to analyze the population dynamics of raccoons in Germany, annual hunting bag data at administrative district level (412 districts, status 2009), gathered up by the German wildlife information system database (WILD), which is commissioned by the German Hunting Association (Deutscher Jagdverband e.V.), were scanned for 12 hunting seasons from 2000/01 to 2011/12 (hunting seasons cover the time from 1 April to 31 March).

Hauptgruppe_RoteListen.evidence_anchor: As the second largest cause of biodiversity loss worldwide, there is an urgent need to study the dynamics of biological invasions and identify factors limiting the distribution of invasive alien species. In the present study we analyze national-scale hunting bag data from Germany to predict the dispersal of raccoons in the largest non-native population of the species.

Lebensraum.evidence_anchor: Although Germany represents the core of the non-native range in Europe, information about the current status of the raccoon and the patterns of range expansion at a national scale is still rare.

Trend.evidence_anchor: The increase from about 9,000 harvested raccoons in 2000/01 to about 71,000 in 2011/12 reflects the extensive amount of suitable habitat for this omnivorous species in Central Europe.

Untergruppe_RoteListen.evidence_anchor: Raccoons were introduced in different European countries by deliberate or accidental releases occurring since the early twentieth century (Beltrán-Beck et al. 2012).
